title: Streamlit multiselect default options not working when using sequence of custom classes with __str__ method

labels.name: status:unlikely
labels.description: Will probably not implement but looking for feedback

body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When using custom class as a choice option and also giving all the options as default values, we do not get the proper default values selected. The comparison of the default options and the option choices fails, since the class attributes are all the same but the underlying object attributes aren't.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import dataclasses
import streamlit as st

@dataclasses.dataclass
class Choice():
    option1: str = "option 1"
    option2: str = "option 2"
    def __init__(self, name: str) -> None:
        self.name: str = name
    @classmethod
    def get_options(cls) -> List[Any]:  # pyre-ignore[3]
        """Returns a list of all the options."""
        return [cls(col.default) for col in dataclasses.fields(cls)]

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        """Returns name of choice."""
        return self.name

choices = st.multiselect(
            "Sie können einzelne Vorhersagen anzeigen oder ausblenden:",
            Choice.get_options(),
            Choice.get_options(),
        )
print([choice.name for choice in choices])
```


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Copy this code example in jupyter notebook with streamlit installed
2. Run the code example.

### Expected Behavior

It should print ["option 1", "option 2"]

### Current Behavior

It prints ["option 1", "option 1"]

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.17.0
- Python version: 3.8.16
- Operating System: WSL
- Browser: Microsoft edge
- Virtual environment: Conda Env


### Additional Information

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/56148594/233115142-b2c675ed-d8dd-49f2-bd40-9c378a557752.png)

The index returned here in line 102 are  [0, 0]. But it should be [0,1].

This is happening since the object look the same on the surface Choice(option1="option 1", option="option2") even though they have different names
